utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Is there something wrong with your hand?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Why are you turning your fork? It's all dangled. Honestly, the way you’re shoveling that in looks like you were raised in a barn, not in this family.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: That's actually pretty mean, Grandma. It's just a fork, I'm not being 'uncivilized' just because I'm comfortable.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It’s about standards. But you kids don't care about dignity anymore. Now, turn it back. Use the tines to push, don't scoop like a child.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Why is your 'English way' the only right way? Scooping is way more efficient for peas. We’re just arguing over a procedure that doesn't change how the food tastes.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Efficiency is for the kitchen; elegance is for the table. I won't have you eating like an American tourist at my Sunday dinner. We are stopping the meal until you hold it correctly.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Um, I don't know, it's just how I eat. This is how you eat?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Yeah. No, no, no, no. Okay, okay. Like this. I like this, the fork this way. Why would you eat with the fork this way?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I don't know, because it's curved up.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: No. Okay, okay, no. Let me show you. Okay. This is the English way of eating. Okay. Like this. Like this. Cut it like this. And you eat it like this. Not like this.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Okay, okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You want to try?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: yes

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. That's good. Mm-hmm. And now— oh, jump, jump, jump! Jump! Bring the arm in a bit. Bring the arm in a bit. Let me show you again.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Let me show you again. Like this. I'm so stressed. Straight, just straight, straight down. Like that. Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Cut. Straight up. Right. There you go, you're British.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I'm British now!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You're British! Sort of one.
